\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} Annual panel 1996--2023, no microstates. Local projections of 100 $\times$ log GDP per capita from t $-$ 1 to t + h on a wage bill shock (percentage points of GDP), with two lags of the shock and of growth and country and year fixed effects; h = $-$1 is zero by construction. Shocks: (a) 100 $\times$ (W\_{t$-$1}/P\_{t$-$2} $-$ W\_{t$-$2}/P\_{t$-$2}) / y\_{t$-$2}, dated in t $-$ 1 and deflated by the deflator of t $-$ 2, so it uses no current prices or output; (b) residual of the current shock (100 $\times$ (W\_t/P\_t $-$ W\_{t$-$1}/P\_{t$-$1}) / y\_{t$-$1}) on current growth and two lags, with country-specific slopes and country and year fixed effects; (c) the current shock deflated by the deflator of t $-$ 1. Inference: Driscoll-Kraay standard errors (maximum lag 3); lag-augmented local projections (Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Møller, 2021: one more lag of the shock and of growth, heteroskedasticity-robust errors); half-panel jackknife bias correction (2 $\times$ full sample $-$ mean of 1996--2009 and 2010--2023), with the full-sample Driscoll-Kraay standard error. Shock (b) is a generated regressor: its standard errors and 95\% CIs come from a country block bootstrap that re-estimates the purging regression in each of 999 replications (percentile CI in the first column; lag-augmented column with robust errors that ignore the generated-regressor step). Panel B: shock (a) interacted with merit above the median in t $-$ 2 (V-Dem), with the total shock as control, so the coefficient is high $-$ low; Romano--Wolf step-down p over h = 0--6, 999 country draws. Stars from the standard errors of each column; 95\% CIs in brackets. Exploratory (pre-registered in the first addendum). * p<0.10, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01. Shock (a), h = 2: Driscoll-Kraay p = 0.0095 (below 0.01). With the half-panel jackknife, the lead at h = $-$2 is $-$0.078 (p = 0.070), significant at 10%.\end{minipage}
\end{table}

\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} Shocks (a), (b) and (c) of Table A16; annual panel 1996--2023, country and year fixed effects, two lags of the shock and of growth. Wage-bill response: change in the wage bill (\% of GDP) from t $-$ 2 to t + h on shock (a), dated t $-$ 1; Driscoll-Kraay 95\% CI. Multiplier: cumulative change in log real GDP per capita ($\times$100, from t $-$ 1, summed over horizons 0 to h) on the cumulative change in the wage bill (points of GDP, from t $-$ 2 for shock (a) and from t $-$ 1 for shocks (b) and (c), summed over 0 to h), instrumented by the shock (LP-IV, Ramey and Zubairy, 2018); Driscoll-Kraay standard errors (bandwidth 4) and normal 95\% CI; shock (b) is a generated regressor and its CIs are percentiles of a country block bootstrap that redoes the purge (999 replications; its standard error is the interquartile range of the bootstrap draws divided by 1.349, because draws with a near-zero first stage produce extreme ratios). F: Kleibergen-Paap robust first-stage F (one instrument); values below 10 indicate a weak instrument, and the multipliers and their CIs are then unreliable. θ/5: coefficient of the change in log GDP per capita ($\times$100) from t $-$ 1 to t + 5 on the mean change of the wage bill over h = 0--5, instrumented by the shock, divided by 5 (delta-method CI); dividing by 6, the number of growth years, gives values five-sixths as large. The preferred specification: the five-year coefficient ($-$0.142) and its 90\% CI. Exploratory (post-plan, pre-registered in the second addendum).\end{minipage}
